keyVerseText: Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord GOD.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun זָכוּר (zâkûwr) is a masculine form derived as a passive participle from the root זָכַר (zâkar), which fundamentally means to remember, mark, or be male. While זָכַר itself carries a range of meanings including to recall or make mention, זָכוּר specifically designates a male individual, particularly emphasizing the biological or generational aspect of maleness. This root connection enriches the term beyond a mere gender marker, suggesting an identity marked or recognized within a community or covenant context.
usageInScripture: The word זָכוּר appears four times in Scripture, consistently translated with reference to males or men, such as "all thy males" or "every male." Its usage spans contexts including communal religious attendance and warfare, as seen in references to males attending feasts or being distinguished from women and children in military commands. This consistency underscores its role as a collective term for male members of a group, often in covenantal or societal settings.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding זָכוּר highlights the biblical emphasis on male identity within covenantal and communal life, reflecting God’s ordering of relationships and responsibilities. The term’s root in remembrance and marking invites reflection on how males are not only biological but also covenantally recognized persons called to represent family and community before God. This recognition points forward to the incarnate Son of God, who fulfills and transcends human identity. Moreover, the inclusion of all males in covenantal acts underscores the corporate nature of faith and obedience in the Old Testament, which finds its ultimate fulfillment in Christ’s mediation for all people.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 23:17 states, "Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord GOD." Here, זָכוּר emphasizes the collective gathering of all male members of Israel to worship, symbolizing their communal responsibility and identity before God. This word highlights the inclusivity of male participation in covenantal worship, reminding believers that God calls His people to come before Him in unity and remembrance. It points to the importance of corporate faithfulness and the visible presence of God’s covenant community.
